items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Felix was also in touch with an American tenor sax man named Fred Palmer... That was no worhty recommendation to me, but it was Felix who was really forming this orchestra that I was to lead.

ctx.x: I became acquainted with some Philippine musicians but how this happened, I do not recall. However, it happened and one who played trombone called himself Felix the Cat. He had played in Japan before the war and told me that he had been associated with an American trombone player known as Slick. I had known Slick also because he had been in Cincinnati for a while and he also played trumpet. He was the first trumpet player I had ever known that played trombone or visa versa, But I never knew his real name.

Felix played with an orchestra, all Philippines, that had 16 musicians. And if you closed your eyes or only heard them playing if you were coming into a dance hall, you would bet your bottom dollar that it was the Glenn Miller band playing an engagement while passing through Manila. The only weakness was in the solos. But the sound was there.

We were invited to a few local spots where they would play now and then and I would sit in with them a few times. They gave me all the brass solo parts and I gave them everything I could because I was really getting my kicks playing with a big band and hearing good harmony, accompanying me. And the musicians were getting their kicks listening to me because they had no soloists of any value in the trumpet section and it pleased them to hear something played as it would have been in the States by jazz musicians or…
